# Segler Ink

> Segler Ink is building an e-ink device that gives up nothing to LCD and OLED screens, and beats them with everything e-ink does better. The project is a privately run prototype, built on the open Modos Labs Glider platform.

## Why a fast e-ink tablet

- Fast enough to be a tablet: scrolling, typing, drawing and video that keep up with the hand. A full tablet, not an ereader you put up with.
- Easy on the eyes: the image is made of physical ink, not glowing pixels, and the matte surface keeps glare low. A built-in light is there when the room is dark.
- Clearer in sunlight: the screen reflects ambient light the way paper does. Outdoors it gets easier to read instead of washing out.
- Power only when the page changes: e-ink holds an image without power. A still page costs almost nothing to keep on screen; only changes draw power.
- Open foundation: built on the Modos Labs Glider, an open e-ink platform, rather than a closed system.

## Targets

Design targets for the prototype, not measured results.

- Refresh rate: 60 Hz+
- Input latency: under 30 ms
- Panel: monochrome
- Battery: days

## The name

Segler is German for a sailboat, and for a glider: fluid, smooth and fast. The name also nods to the Modos Labs Glider, the open e-ink platform this project builds on.
